$comment: What an element does to a human body, and how it gets there. The fifth curated field, after roles, homonyms, inert and needs, and for the same reason as the other four: it is a fact about the thing that no tag, no recipe and no heuristic can supply. It exists so the Ragdoll canvas can answer 'what happens if this touches a person' from checked data rather than from invention.
$rules: route is the axis a hazard list does not have and a body does. The same substance is inert on skin, dangerous inhaled and lethal injected, because each route meets different barriers and reaches the blood at a different rate. Asbestos in a wall is not a hazard; asbestos in the air is.

outcome must name an element this corpus already has. That is what makes this layer checkable: the outcome card is an ordinary element card, already through validate, sources, roles and the audit. If an outcome does not exist yet, author it as ordinary corpus work first.

mechanism describes WHAT HAPPENS IN THE BODY and never how to bring it about. No procedure, no quantity that would cause harm, no way to obtain or concentrate anything. tools/effects.mjs fails the build on method-shaped prose rather than warning, because a check that only warns about this is worse than none.

onset uses the same four tiers as data/cautions.json — acute, contact, conditional, cumulative — because that vocabulary already existed and already fits. cumulative is the one a damage simulation cannot do: a carcinogen does nothing visible on contact, and the honest canvas shows a clock rather than a wound.
carcinogen: true is for IARC Group 1 only. Nothing weaker gets the word.
every effect carries a src, like every other claim in this corpus.

a verb is not an element, so verbs live in their own block. The Ragdoll has to answer smother the same way it answers methane — the brief asked for it in those words — and the five that act on a body get the same route, onset, mechanism and source as any substance.

an element carries a LIST of effects, not one, because the same thing is routinely both. Sun makes vitamin D in the skin and melanoma in the same skin, by the same route, from the same photons; salt is required and salt raises blood pressure. A field that could only hold the harm was a hazard list wearing a body's clothes, and it made the corpus look as though nothing on it was good for anyone.
valence says which side an entry is on, because a machine cannot read it off the outcome and the canvas has to colour it. carcinogen is meaningless on a benefit and the gate rejects it there.

prevents is optional and names the deficiency disease this thing keeps away — an element like any other, so scurvy, rickets and goitre are all cards you can already open. outcome stays 'what the body gets'; prevents is 'what it is spared'.

the benefit side has a denominator too, and it is external rather than ours: $nutrients is the list of things a human body cannot make and must be given. A nutrient is covered when some element in this corpus carries a benefit row whose outcome IS that nutrient. Without a written denominator this half of the field could sit at thirty rows for a year and nothing would show that it had — which is exactly what happened to needs.

an effect can belong to the HAZARD rather than to each of its elements. data/cautions.json already attaches its wording to the hazard and not to the item — 'so it reads the same everywhere on a chain' — and the same is true of the effect: what beryllium dust does to a lung is one fact about beryllium dust, not twelve facts about twelve alloys. The `hazards` block writes it once and every id on that hazard's list answers with it. A row in `effects` for a particular element always wins, because that is where a thing deserves its own answer.

stages are the dose. A thing is not simply good or bad for a body, it is good or bad AT SOMETHING — sun for ten minutes and sun for four hours are different facts about the same star. Where a real, published staging exists, an entry carries a `dial` naming what is actually being measured and a `stages` ladder along it. The scale must be the one the medicine uses (core temperature, carboxyhaemoglobin per cent, burn degree), never an invented 0-to-100, and never an amount of a substance to take: a ladder is what happens as exposure grows, not instructions for growing it.

a rung may carry its own valence. The sun's ladder runs from a hormone being built to a lifetime melanoma risk, and it is one ladder because it is one exposure getting longer — so the rung decides whether the card is green or not, and the entry it hangs off only decides where it is written down.

inert is a third valence and it is not the same as silence. Gold in a body does nothing, and saying so is a real fact with a real reason behind it; saying nothing is an admission that nobody has looked. An inert row needs no outcome, because there is no outcome.

an outcome has a SITE and a SIGN. Route says how a thing gets in; it says nothing about what the body then does, so every outcome looked identical on the canvas — a burn, a brain tumour and a drowning all produced the same nothing. `outcomes` gives each one the organ it acts on and the one visible thing that is true of it, from a closed vocabulary. The site must be an element, so it is checkable like everything else.

the cumulative rule outranks the sign. A carcinogen's outcome may have a sign, and a cumulative exposure still shows the clock and nothing else — asbestos on a body does nothing today whatever mesothelioma looks like. This is the rule the whole layer was built around and no sign may override it.

$valence.harm: the body is worse off for the encounter
$valence.benefit: the body is better off for it — a nutrient it cannot make, a deficiency disease it prevents, a function it enables
$valence.inert: the body is unchanged by it, and that is a fact about the thing rather than a gap in the record — the reason it can be left inside a person

$routes.inhaled: reaches the blood through the lung, which has the surface area of a tennis court and no barrier worth the name
$routes.ingested: goes through the gut and then the liver, which processes it before the rest of the body sees it
$routes.contact: acts where it lands; skin is a real barrier and most things stop there
$routes.absorbed: crosses intact skin and reaches the blood — a short list, and the reason gloves are specified by chemical
$routes.injected: bypasses every barrier, which is why the same dose behaves differently
$routes.mechanical: does its damage by force rather than chemistry
$routes.thermal: damages by temperature, in either direction

$signs.pulse: the site throbs — something is growing, inflamed, or hurting there
$signs.flush: the site changes colour — blood arriving, blood leaving, or a pigment laid down
$signs.mark: a lesion appears at the site and stays
$signs.still: the part stops moving, because the signal to it has stopped
$signs.shiver: rapid small movement — shivering, fasciculation, a seizure
$signs.slack: the body loses its hold and falls. Reserved for death, and nothing else may use it
$signs.wait: nothing is visible now, and that is the honest depiction

$nutrients_comment: Essential nutrients: the things a human body cannot synthesise, or cannot synthesise fast enough, and must take in. The list is not ours — it is the standard one, and that is the point of using it as a denominator. Four of them have no element in this corpus yet (pantothenic acid and the two essential fatty acids), so they cannot be covered until one is authored; they stay on the list so the gap is visible rather than quietly absent. chloride is carried by the element `chlorine`, and vitamin B12 by `cobalamin`, because those are the ids this corpus has.

vitamin_a.why: Retinal is the light-absorbing half of rhodopsin; there is no substitute for it in the eye.

thiamin.why: The cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase — without it a cell cannot get sugar into the citric acid cycle at all.

riboflavin.why: The backbone of FAD and FMN, the carriers half of oxidative metabolism runs on.

niacin.why: Becomes NAD, which is on one side or the other of most reactions in the body.

pantothenic_acid.why: Becomes coenzyme A. No element for it in this corpus yet — author it before this can be covered.

vitamin_b6.why: The cofactor for transaminases, so it sits under nearly all amino acid chemistry.

biotin.why: Carries carbon dioxide for the carboxylases; the gut makes some, not enough.

folate.why: Moves single carbon atoms, which is most of what building DNA consists of.

cobalamin.why: Vitamin B12. Made only by bacteria and archaea — no plant or animal synthesises it.

vitamin_c.why: The gene for the last enzyme in its pathway is broken in us, so collagen cannot be cross-linked without eating it.

vitamin_d.why: Strictly a hormone the skin makes from sunlight, and a nutrient only where the sun will not do it.

vitamin_e.why: The fat-soluble antioxidant that sits in membranes and is oxidised instead of the lipids around it.

vitamin_k.why: Required to finish the clotting factors; without it they are made and do not work.

calcium.why: Bone is the bank, but the reason the level is defended so hard is that muscle and nerve spend it.

phosphorus.why: In every ATP, every nucleotide and most of the mineral in bone.

potassium.why: The ion inside the cell, as sodium is the ion outside it.

sodium.why: Every nerve impulse is a sodium gradient collapsing and being rebuilt.

chlorine.why: Chloride: the counter-ion to sodium, and the acid in the stomach.

magnesium.why: ATP is only usable as a magnesium complex, so it is a cofactor for hundreds of enzymes at once.

iron.why: The atom oxygen binds to in haemoglobin. Nothing else in the body does that job.

zinc.why: Structural in a whole class of transcription factors, and required for wound repair and taste.

iodine.why: The thyroid hormones are built around iodine atoms and cannot be built without them.

selenium.why: Sits in the active site of glutathione peroxidase as selenocysteine, the twenty-first amino acid.

copper.why: In cytochrome c oxidase at the end of the respiratory chain, and in the enzyme that cross-links collagen.

manganese.why: The metal in the superoxide dismutase inside mitochondria.

molybdenum.why: Needed by exactly four human enzymes, and deficiency is almost unknown — which is itself the fact.

chromium.why: Trivalent chromium, in trace amounts, in glucose handling — and the most contested entry on this list.

histidine.why: Essential in infancy and, on the current view, in adults too.

isoleucine.why: One of the three branched-chain amino acids, burned in muscle rather than liver.

leucine.why: The one that signals as well as builds: it switches on muscle protein synthesis directly.

lysine.why: The limiting amino acid in cereals, and the reason a grain alone is not enough.

methionine.why: Starts every protein and donates methyl groups; the limiting one in legumes.

phenylalanine.why: The precursor of tyrosine and so of dopamine, adrenaline and melanin.

threonine.why: Heavily used in mucin, so the gut lining spends it faster than most tissues.

tryptophan.why: The precursor of serotonin and of niacin, and the rarest essential amino acid in food.

valine.why: The third branched-chain amino acid; the one substitution that causes sickle cell is a valine.

linoleic_acid.why: Omega-6. No element for it in this corpus yet — author it before this can be covered.

alpha_linolenic_acid.why: Omega-3. No element for it in this corpus yet — author it before this can be covered.

choline.why: Needed for cell membranes and acetylcholine; the body makes some and not enough.

$verbs_comment: The verbs that do something to a body. Keys are ids from data/verbs.json, not elements. wait, ferment and blow are absent on purpose: none of them does anything to a person on the timescale the canvas shows.
$hazards_comment: Keyed on data/cautions.json's own hazard ids. Each row is what that class of hazard does to a body, and it answers for every element on that hazard's list. This is not a shortcut around authoring: it is the right grain. Where an element deserves a specific answer it gets a row of its own in `effects`, which overrides this entirely.
$outcomes_comment: What the body visibly does, per outcome. `site` is an element — an organ or tissue this corpus already has — so the anatomy is checkable rather than asserted in a switch statement. `sign` is one of $signs. This is not a damage model: it depicts the sign that is recorded, and a cumulative exposure shows the clock regardless of what its outcome's sign is.
$no_effect_rule: effects-common counts the two hundred most-used elements, and a good part of that list cannot meet a body at all. An IDEA (language, evolution, time, natural selection), a PROCESS OF HISTORY (harvest, speciation), a POLITY or BELIEF (country, buddhism), a PART OF THE BODY ITSELF (skin, heart, nerve, eye, muscle, tissue, cell), a SUB-CELLULAR OR CHEMICAL ABSTRACTION (dna, gene, mutation, membrane, atp), a PLACE (island, rainforest, field), or something EXTINCT (dinosaur) owes no effect row. Counting them made the metric look permanently unfinishable, which is the same fault $not_assemblies fixed for needs. This is a list of things that cannot have an answer — NOT a list of things whose answer is 'nothing'. Where a thing really does meet a body and does nothing, that is an `inert` row with a reason, not an entry here.

aconite.mechanism: Aconitine keeps sodium channels open and the heart is what shows it. The alkaloid crosses intact skin, which is the property that made it a poison of choice long before anyone could name the mechanism.

air.mechanism: A fifth oxygen, four fifths nitrogen, and the nitrogen is not filler — it dilutes the oxygen to a partial pressure lungs can tolerate. Pure oxygen at the same pressure damages the airway lining.

akee.mechanism: Hypoglycin A blocks the body from burning fat, so it must run on glucose alone and the blood sugar falls to nothing. The fruit is safe once it has opened on the tree by itself; picked before that, it is not.

almond.mechanism: One of the densest sources of alpha-tocopherol there is, in the fat where it is needed and stays stable.

aloe_vera.mechanism: The clear gel in the middle of the leaf and the yellow latex just under the rind are two different substances. Aloin is in the latex, it is a stimulant laxative, and it is why whole-leaf preparations behave nothing like gel.

aluminum.mechanism: It grows a passivating oxide film within milliseconds of meeting air, and that film — not the metal — is what everything touches. It is the reason aluminium cookware does not dissolve into food.

ammonia.mechanism: It is extremely soluble in water, so it is captured by the first wet surface it meets — eyes and upper airway — and makes a strong alkali on the spot. That is also why it warns so effectively: nobody stays in it by accident.

apple.mechanism: Modest per fruit and eaten in quantity, which is how most of Europe got it before citrus was cheap. The vitamin sits mostly just under the skin, so peeling removes a good part of it.

apricot.mechanism: The flesh is food and has nothing to do with this. The kernel inside the stone carries amygdalin, and a gut's own enzymes are what release the cyanide from it — bitter kernels run several per cent amygdalin, sweet ones a fraction of that.

arch.mechanism: An arch stands only while every block in it stays in compression, and the load it is holding is masonry. Crush syndrome is what arrives when a person is trapped under fallen masonry: it is not the local injury but a systemic one, shock and kidney failure from muscle that was compressed rather than broken.

asbestos.mechanism: The fibres split lengthwise rather than across, so they are narrow enough to reach the deep lung and long enough that a macrophage cannot engulf one. They stay, and the irritation continues for decades. In a wall it is inert; the hazard is entirely airborne.

automobile.mechanism: Around a million people a year, and the injury is deceleration rather than impact: the body stops with the car and the organs inside it do not, which is why the damage is often internal and invisible.

autumn_crocus.mechanism: Colchicine stops cells from dividing by preventing the mitotic spindle from forming, so the tissues that turn over fastest fail first — gut lining and bone marrow. There is no antidote.

bacteria.mechanism: Most bacteria are harmless and a great many are necessary — there are more of them in a person than there are human cells. The pathogenic ones differ by a handful of acquired genes rather than by being a different sort of thing.

banana.mechanism: Potassium is the ion inside the cell as sodium is the ion outside it, and every heartbeat depends on the difference being maintained.

bark.mechanism: Not a vitamin source in general — but the one that mattered: spruce and pine bark and needles carried enough ascorbic acid to end scurvy on voyages where citrus was unavailable, which is what Cartier's crew were given at Stadacona in 1536.

bean.mechanism: Lysine is the amino acid cereals run out of first, and legumes are full of it. That is why beans and a grain turn up together on nearly every continent: neither is complete and the pair is.

beef.mechanism: Haem iron, already inside a porphyrin ring, which the gut takes up by a different route from plant iron and far more completely. Without enough, the marrow cannot fill red cells with haemoglobin.

benzene.mechanism: It is metabolised into reactive intermediates that damage bone marrow, where blood cells are made. The association with leukaemia is why it was removed from consumer products.

betel_nut.mechanism: Chewed with or without tobacco, the areca nut is itself carcinogenic — the cancers are of the mouth, pharynx and oesophagus, the tissue it sits against. It is among the most widely used psychoactive substances in the world.

bird_wing.mechanism: A swan defending a nest really does strike with its wings, which carry bony spurs, and the blow is frightening. It is also the origin of the most durable animal myth in Britain: the wings are not strong enough to break an adult man's leg, however often that is repeated. A wing is hollow bone and feather, built to the lightest specification that will still fly, and the same design that makes it efficient is what limits what it can deliver.

blood.mechanism: Blood is the route for the pathogens that cannot survive drying — hepatitis B and C, and HIV. Intact skin is a complete barrier to all of them; a break in it is not.

bone.mechanism: A swallowed fish bone is one of the commonest foreign bodies in an oesophagus. It is thin enough to pass the throat and stiff enough to lodge point-first, and the danger is perforation rather than obstruction.

book.mechanism: Cellulose and ink. There is nothing in a book a human gut can take apart, which is why the fibre in a plant and the fibre in a page are the same problem.

bracken_fern.mechanism: Ptaquiloside is water-soluble and survives into milk from grazing animals as well as into the fern itself. The link is to tumours in livestock and to human oesophageal and gastric cancer where young fronds are eaten as a vegetable.

brain.mechanism: The one tissue where eating it has transmitted a disease with no organism in it at all. A prion is a misfolded protein that makes copies of its own misfolding, and nothing that destroys a bacterium or a virus touches it.

brass.mechanism: Free-machining brass carries a few per cent lead to make it cut cleanly, and a brass fitting on a drinking-water line is in permanent contact with what passes through it. That is what lead-free plumbing standards exist to limit.

brazil_nut.mechanism: Selenium sits in the active site of glutathione peroxidase as selenocysteine, the twenty-first amino acid, coded by a stop codon read differently. Brazil nuts take it up from the soil, so the amount in a nut varies with where the tree grew rather than with the nut.

bread.mechanism: Starch gelatinised by baking is far easier for amylase to reach than raw flour, which is most of why cooking cereal was worth the fuel. Around half the calories eaten by humanity arrive as some form of this.

brick.mechanism: The fired clay is harmless in one piece. Cutting and grinding it releases respirable crystalline silica, and the lung has no way to clear a particle it cannot dissolve.

broccoli.mechanism: More ascorbic acid by weight than an orange, though boiling leaches it into the water. The vitamin is the same molecule whatever it arrives in.

Trivalent chromium in trace amounts, associated with insulin's action on the cell. It is the most contested entry on any essential-nutrient list, and broccoli is the food usually named — both facts belong on the card.

bromine.mechanism: A liquid at room temperature that boils readily, so the hazard is a heavy red-brown vapour. It oxidises tissue on contact and, like chlorine, generates acid in the airway lining.

cabbage.mechanism: Brassicas carry glucosinolates that interfere with the thyroid's uptake of iodine. It matters only where iodine is already short, and cooking reduces it — which is why this is a fact about diets rather than about cabbage.

carbon.mechanism: Elemental carbon is about as biologically unavailable as matter gets. Activated charcoal passes through a gut adsorbing things and is not itself absorbed, and tattoo pigment is carbon that stays in the dermis for a lifetime without being recognised.

carbon_dioxide.mechanism: Unlike most asphyxiants it is not silent. The urge to breathe answers carbon dioxide directly, so a rising level produces real air hunger and panic — which is why carbon monoxide kills people who feel fine and this does not.

carbon_monoxide.mechanism: It binds haemoglobin far more tightly than oxygen does and will not let go, so the blood is still circulating and no longer carrying. It is odourless, and the early symptoms are a headache and confusion, which is not a combination that makes people leave a building.

dial.note: The fraction of haemoglobin holding carbon monoxide instead of oxygen.

stages.label: Ordinary air
stages.what: Everyone carries a little. A non-smoker sits at one or two per cent from ordinary metabolism and traffic.

stages.label: Headache
stages.what: The first symptom, and indistinguishable from every other headache — which is the whole danger. Nothing about the gas can be smelled or seen.

stages.label: Confusion
stages.what: Judgement goes before strength does, so the person who most needs to leave the building is the least able to decide to.

stages.label: Collapse
stages.what: Blood is still circulating, still red, and no longer carrying. The pulse oximeter reads normal because it cannot tell the two bound forms apart.

stages.label: Unsurvivable without treatment
stages.what: At this fraction there is not enough carrying capacity left to supply the brain.

carrot.mechanism: Beta-carotene, split in the gut wall into two molecules of retinal. The conversion is regulated, which is the reason a plant source does not overshoot the way stored retinol can.

cashew.mechanism: A cashew is not a nut and its shell is not a shell: it is a drupe whose casing holds anacardic acid, the same chemical family as the resin in poison ivy. The roasting a cashew reaches you already done is what destroys it.

cheese.mechanism: The calcium follows the curd rather than the whey, so it concentrates as the water leaves — one of the few foods where processing raises the mineral density.
Phosphorus is in every ATP, every nucleotide and most of the mineral in bone. In cheese it comes bound to casein, which keeps it soluble as the curd dries.

chicken.mechanism: Muscle eaten to build muscle: the filaments are broken to amino acids in the gut and reassembled to a different specification on the other side.

chickpea.mechanism: B6 becomes pyridoxal phosphate, the cofactor every transaminase uses, so it sits underneath nearly all amino acid chemistry rather than beside it.

clay.mechanism: Geophagia is documented across cultures and pregnancies, and kaolin does bind some toxins and pathogens in the gut. It also binds iron and zinc, so the practice can cause the deficiency it is sometimes an appetite for.

clostridium_botulinum.mechanism: It grows only where there is no oxygen, little acid and warmth, and what it produces then blocks the signal from nerve to muscle. The conditions that suit it are exactly the ones that home preserving creates, which is why the hazard sits with the method rather than the food.

cloth.mechanism: Cotton dust causes byssinosis, and its signature is that the chest tightness comes back on the first day of the working week and eases through it. Nineteenth-century mills called it Monday fever long before anyone knew what caused it.

cocoa.mechanism: ATP is only usable by an enzyme as a magnesium complex, so magnesium is a cofactor for hundreds of reactions at once rather than a specialist. Cocoa solids are among the densest food sources there are.

coffee.mechanism: Caffeine does not supply energy. It occupies the receptors adenosine uses to report how long you have been awake, so the tiredness is not removed, only unreported — and it is still owed when the caffeine clears.

coin.mechanism: Nickel released by sweat binds skin protein, and the immune system learns the combination permanently. Handling coins is the classic occupational exposure — cashiers were the first group in whom it was described.

concrete.mechanism: Wet cement is strongly alkaline and it does not sting, so kneeling in it can produce a full-thickness burn over hours without any warning at the time. Set concrete is inert; the hazard is entirely in the window while it is curing.

copper.mechanism: Freshly formed metal-oxide fume is fine enough to reach the deep lung, where it provokes a flu-like reaction that comes on hours after the work and is gone the next day. It is the metal in fume form, not the metal in hand.

copper_wire.mechanism: Metallic copper releases too little into dry skin to matter, which is why copper wire is handled bare all day. Its salts are another matter, and the fume from heating it is another again.

coral.mechanism: A coral cut is shallow and heals badly, because the wound is seeded with fragments of skeleton and with the marine bacteria living on them. Fire corals are not corals at all but hydroids, and they sting rather than cut.

cow.mechanism: Cattle kill more people each year than sharks or snakes in most countries that keep them, and almost always by crushing rather than goring — a cow that leans on a handler against a rail weighs more than the rail will give.

current.mechanism: It is current that injures, not voltage: the path and the amount decide it. Milliamps across the chest can fibrillate a heart, and the skin's resistance, which is what usually limits it, falls by an order of magnitude when wet.

cyanide.mechanism: It stops the enzyme at the end of the respiratory chain, so cells cannot use oxygen even though the blood is full of it. The person is hypoxic with red venous blood, which is the diagnostic oddity.

death_cap.mechanism: The amatoxins are thermostable, so cooking changes nothing, and they shut down RNA polymerase II — the liver is the organ that concentrates them. The cruelty is the gap: the first symptoms remit, and the person appears to recover while the damage continues.

desert.mechanism: Sweating works until the water runs out, and then the core temperature has nothing left holding it down. Dry air hides how much is being lost, because it evaporates before it is felt.

dog.mechanism: A bite is an injection of mouth flora past every barrier the skin has. Pasteurella and Capnocytophaga are ordinary in a healthy dog's mouth, and a puncture from a canine tooth seals over the top of them.

drupe.mechanism: The stone is hardened ovary wall, and inside it the kernel of most stone fruit carries amygdalin. Crushing releases hydrogen cyanide; swallowing a stone whole does not, which is why the flesh is food and the pit is a caution.

earth.mechanism: The planet is not a thing that meets a body — what meets a body is soil, water, air or sunlight, and each of those is filed on its own. This row exists so the canvas says that rather than nothing.

egg.mechanism: The reference against which other proteins are scored, because the amino acid proportions are close to what a body building tissue actually asks for.

Biotin carries carbon dioxide for the carboxylase enzymes. The yolk is a good source and the raw white is the opposite: avidin in it binds biotin so tightly that it goes straight through. Cooking denatures the avidin and the problem with it.

Choline goes into every cell membrane as phosphatidylcholine and into acetylcholine, the transmitter at every neuromuscular junction. The body makes some and not enough, and the yolk is the densest ordinary source.

electricity.mechanism: Voltage drives current through the body's resistance, and a path across the chest can put enough through the heart to fibrillate it. Hand to hand is worse than hand to foot, and wet skin drops resistance by an order of magnitude.

enzyme.mechanism: Proteolytic enzymes added to washing powder in the 1960s caused an outbreak of occupational asthma in the workers making it — an enzyme is a protein, and inhaling a protein in quantity is how the immune system is taught to react to it.

ethanol.mechanism: The liver converts it to acetaldehyde and then to acetate, and the intermediate is the damaging one. Sustained exposure scars the tissue doing the processing.

feather.mechanism: The same mechanism as farmer's lung, from bird protein in the dust of droppings and feathers. It is called bird fancier's lung and it appears in people who keep pigeons and budgerigars for years.

fire.mechanism: Protein denatures above about 44 °C given long enough, so depth is temperature and time together rather than temperature alone. A low heat held against skin does what a brief high one does.

fish.mechanism: Less connective tissue than land meat, so it flakes rather than needing long cooking — and the same protein arrives either way.

flint.mechanism: It fractures conchoidally, like glass, so a struck flake carries an edge sharper than most steel. That is what made it the first tool material and it has not stopped being true.

flower.mechanism: The plants that cause hay fever are the ones with no flower worth looking at. A showy flower is advertising to insects, so its pollen is heavy, sticky and stays where it is put; wind-pollinated plants make theirs light and in enormous quantity, and that is the pollen in the air.

fly_agaric.mechanism: Muscimol acts directly on the nervous system as a GABA analogue, and ibotenic acid alongside it does the opposite. What follows is delirium and altered consciousness rather than organ damage, which is why the two are so often confused in accounts of it.

formaldehyde.mechanism: It cross-links protein on contact, which is what makes it a fixative and what makes it an irritant to the airway lining at low concentrations.

fossil.mechanism: The organic material is gone. What is left is mineral that has replaced it, so a fossil is a rock in the shape of a thing rather than any of the thing.

foxglove.mechanism: Cardiac glycosides slow the heart by blocking the sodium-potassium pump in its muscle. It is the same action as the drug derived from it, and the margin between the dose that treats and the dose that kills is one of the narrowest in medicine.

frame.mechanism: The cruelty of a frame coming down on someone is in the rescue. While the weight is on, crushed muscle holds its potassium and myoglobin in place; lifting it releases both into the circulation at once, which is why the condition was once called smiling death. UK first-aid guidance tells untrained rescuers not to free anyone who has been trapped more than fifteen minutes.

frost.mechanism: Freezing is not simply cold. Water crystallises between and then inside cells, and it is the crystal edges that do the damage — which is why rapid rewarming hurts and slow rewarming injures more.

fruit.mechanism: Humans carry a broken copy of the last enzyme in the vitamin C pathway, so it has to arrive in food. Fruit is where most people get it, and cooking is what destroys it.

fungus.mechanism: Most fungi cannot grow at body temperature, which is a large part of why so few of the millions of species trouble us. The ones that do are either kept to the dead outer skin or take hold only where the immune system has stepped back.

gamma_ray.mechanism: It ionises as it passes, damaging DNA, and the tissues that replace themselves fastest show it first — marrow, gut lining, hair follicles. There is often a latent period of apparent recovery before the marrow fails.

giant_hogweed.mechanism: The sap alone does nothing. Furanocoumarins in it bind DNA in the skin and only then does sunlight break the bond, so the burn appears a day or two after contact and recurs on the same skin for years afterwards.

glacier.mechanism: A crevasse is bridged by snow that looks like the rest of the surface, and a fall into one wedges a body tighter the deeper it goes. What follows is the cold: the walls are ice on every side and there is no way to move.

glass.mechanism: It fractures without deforming, so a break leaves an edge rather than a dent, and that edge is sharp at the scale of a cell. The wound is clean and deep for the force involved.

glucose.mechanism: The one fuel the brain will use in ordinary circumstances, at about a fifth of the body's whole energy budget for two per cent of its weight. It is also the only sugar the blood carries — everything else is converted first.

gold.mechanism: Metallic gold does not oxidise, does not dissolve in body fluids, and releases no ions for the immune system to react to. That is why it has been left inside people for centuries — in teeth, in eyelid weights, in the wire of an implant — and why almost nobody is allergic to it.

grain.mechanism: Starch is glucose stored in a form a plant can pack tightly and a gut can take apart again. Cereals supply about half the calories eaten by the human species, which is why a bad harvest is a historical event rather than a dietary one.

granite.mechanism: Granite carries traces of uranium, and uranium decays through radium to radon — a gas, which is the part that matters. It seeps out of the rock and collects in enclosed spaces below ground, and it is the leading cause of lung cancer in people who have never smoked.

grass.mechanism: Grass pollen is wind-carried, which means it is made in enormous quantity and is small enough to stay airborne — both of which are why it is the commonest cause of hay fever. The immune system has learned a protein that is doing nothing to it.

gunpowder.mechanism: It deflagrates rather than detonating — it burns very fast rather than producing a supersonic shock — so the injury is flame and hot gas, and the hazard scales with confinement.

hammer.mechanism: A hammer works by delivering its momentum in a very short time, and a bone answers the same physics as a nail: it fails in bending long before it fails in compression.

holly.mechanism: The berries carry saponins, and children eating them is the usual case. The reputation for lethality is not borne out — vomiting is the ordinary outcome.

honey.mechanism: It draws water out of the wound bed by osmosis and holds a low pH, and bee-derived glucose oxidase releases hydrogen peroxide slowly rather than all at once. Medical-grade honey dressings are a licensed treatment, not a folk remedy.

It can carry Clostridium botulinum spores. An adult gut is too competitive for them; an infant gut under a year old is not, so the spores germinate and produce the toxin inside the child. The honey itself is unchanged — the difference is entirely the gut it lands in.

horse.mechanism: Half a tonne with a kick delivered by the strongest muscle group in the animal, at head height for a standing person. Horse-related injuries are among the most serious in any sport, and most of them happen on the ground rather than in the saddle.

horse_chestnut.mechanism: Aesculin, in the seed, the leaf and the flower. The conker is the thing that looks most like food and is the part that carries most of it, which is the whole reason this plant is a childhood hazard rather than an agricultural one.

horsetail.mechanism: It carries thiaminase, an enzyme that takes vitamin B1 apart. Nothing about the plant is directly poisonous; the harm is a deficiency it induces, and it takes sustained eating to arrive — which is why it is a livestock problem rather than a human one.

human.mechanism: Person to person is how most human pathogens travel, and the ones that specialise in us have nowhere else to live — measles, smallpox and polio have no animal reservoir at all. What passes between two people is decided by which surfaces meet and for how long, not by anything either of them intends.

hydrogen.mechanism: Not toxic and not reactive at body temperature. It simply takes the place of air, and because the reflex to breathe answers carbon dioxide rather than oxygen, there is no warning before consciousness goes.

hydrogen_gas.mechanism: It is not toxic and does nothing chemically. It simply takes the place of air, and because the reflex to breathe answers carbon dioxide rather than oxygen, there is no warning before consciousness goes.

ice.mechanism: The body constricts blood flow to the periphery to protect the core, so the extremities freeze while losing their own supply. Thawing hurts far more than freezing, and re-freezing after a thaw is much worse than staying frozen.

ink.mechanism: Tattoo pigment is placed in the dermis and stays there for life, and the immune system meets it continuously. Red pigments account for most reported reactions, often years after the tattoo was made.

insect.mechanism: Insects carry more human disease than any other group of animals, and almost always as a vector rather than as a cause — the mosquito, the tsetse fly and the sandfly are syringes, and what they inject is somebody else's parasite.

iodine.mechanism: Elemental iodine is used as an antiseptic because it is toxic to cells, and skin is made of cells. Tincture stains and stings; the strong solution burns.

iron.mechanism: The body has no way to excrete iron once it is absorbed — intake is regulated at the gut and there is no tap on the other end. A large amount taken at once overwhelms that gate, and free iron in the blood damages the liver and the vessel walls directly. It is a leading cause of poisoning death in small children for exactly this reason: the tablets look like sweets.

kale.mechanism: Folate is named for the leaf it was first pulled out of. It is the cofactor for moving single carbon atoms around, which is most of what building DNA consists of.

kefir.mechanism: A wider mix of bacteria and yeasts than yoghurt, fermented from a grain of them that is reused rather than restarted.

kelp.mechanism: Iodine was first isolated from kelp ash. The gland takes it up against a steep gradient and cannot make the hormone without it.

keratin.mechanism: Hair and nail are dead by the time they are visible: keratin cross-linked by disulphide bonds into something no human enzyme dismantles. That is why cutting either is painless and why they survive in graves.

kimchi.mechanism: The same lactic fermentation, at a lower temperature and over longer, with the bacteria shifting in sequence as the acidity climbs.

larkspur.mechanism: Diterpenoid alkaloids at the neuromuscular junction, concentrated in the young plant and falling as it matures. It kills more cattle on western North American range than any other plant.

larva.mechanism: Many caterpillars carry urticating hairs that break off in skin and release an irritant, and the reaction outlasts the contact by days because the hairs stay in. The adult moth is usually harmless.

lava.mechanism: The same rock once it has reached the surface, cooling but still far above the temperature at which protein denatures. The crust that forms on top is thin and hides how hot what is underneath still is, which is what makes it dangerous to walk on.

lead.mechanism: It is taken up wherever the body wants calcium — into bone, and into the nervous system — because the two ions are similar enough to be confused. It accumulates in bone over years and the damage to a developing nervous system does not reverse.

leather.mechanism: Chrome tanning leaves residual chromium in the hide, and some of it converts to the hexavalent form. Contact dermatitis from shoes is one of the commonest presentations of chromium allergy.

legume.mechanism: Around a quarter protein dry, and short of methionine — which is why the pairing with a grain is not a culinary accident but a completion of the amino acid set.

lemon.mechanism: The same broken enzyme in us, the same fix. Citrus keeps its ascorbic acid well enough to survive a voyage, which is why it and not fresher food solved the problem at sea.

lentil.mechanism: Around a quarter protein dry, and low in methionine — which is why the pairing with a grain is not a culinary accident but a completion of the amino acid set.

Exactly four human enzymes need molybdenum, and legumes carry it because the bacteria in their root nodules need it too, for nitrogenase. Deficiency in a person eating ordinary food is almost unknown, which is itself the interesting part.

lime.mechanism: Humans carry a broken copy of the last enzyme in the vitamin C pathway, so it has to arrive in food. Without it the body cannot cross-link collagen, and every structure that depends on collagen slowly comes apart.

limestone.mechanism: The rock is chalk and harmless to hold. Quarrying and cutting it makes a respirable dust, and the lung's only answer to any insoluble particle is inflammation.

lion.mechanism: A large predator does its damage by force and by tearing rather than by chemistry, and the dangerous injuries are the ones under intact skin.

liver.mechanism: Retinol is stored as an ester in the liver of the animal that ate it, so eating liver delivers the finished vitamin rather than a precursor the gut has to convert. The eye spends it fastest, which is why the first sign of running short is at dusk.

B12 is made by bacteria and archaea and by nothing else alive — no plant and no animal synthesises it. Animals accumulate what their gut flora or their food provides, and the liver is where it is banked, in quantities that last a person years.

lupin.mechanism: Quinolizidine alkaloids, and the reason lupin beans are soaked and rinsed for days before they are eaten. Sweet cultivars have been bred to carry little of it, and the bitterness of the wild ones is a usable warning.

lye.mechanism: It saponifies the fat in skin, so it keeps going deeper for as long as it is present rather than stopping when contact ends. That is why an alkali burn is worse than an acid one of the same strength, and why it needs long irrigation rather than wiping.

mackerel.mechanism: Histidine is essential in infancy and, on the current evidence, in adults too. Oily fish carry a great deal of it in the dark muscle they use for continuous swimming.

The same abundant histidine is what makes this fish dangerous when it has been left warm: bacteria on the flesh decarboxylate it into histamine, which cooking does not destroy because it is not the bacteria that are the problem by then. The reaction that follows looks like an allergy and is not one.

magma.mechanism: Molten rock sits between about 700 and 1,300 °C and carries an enormous amount of heat in very little volume, so contact is not survivable in the way a flame often is. It is also dense enough that a body does not sink into it — the injury is at the surface, and total.

maize.mechanism: The niacin in maize is bound to a carbohydrate the gut cannot open, so a maize diet can be full of it and deliver none. Soaking the grain in an alkali releases it — which is why pellagra followed maize into Europe and the American South, and never appeared in Mesoamerica, where the alkali step was already thousands of years old.

mammal.mechanism: The majority of new human infectious diseases come from other animals, and mammals are the commonest source because our physiology is close enough that their pathogens do not need to change much.

marble.mechanism: Marble itself is calcium carbonate and carries little free silica, but it is quarried and cut alongside stone that does, and the respirable fraction from sawing any of it reaches the alveolus. Engineered stone, sold as a marble substitute, is the worst of them.

mayapple.mechanism: Podophyllotoxin is another spindle poison, and like colchicine its usefulness and its danger are the same property. The ripe fruit is the one part eaten; the rest of the plant is not.

meat.mechanism: Haem iron sits inside a porphyrin ring and crosses the gut wall by its own route, far more completely than the iron in plants. Without enough, the marrow cannot fill red cells with haemoglobin.

mercury.mechanism: Elemental mercury vapour crosses into the brain, where it is oxidised and then cannot cross back out. The metal is nearly harmless swallowed and dangerous breathed, which is the clearest case in this file of route deciding everything.

methane.mechanism: It is not toxic. It displaces oxygen, and the urge to breathe answers carbon dioxide rather than oxygen — so in a methane-rich space the CO2 still leaves normally and there is no warning at all before consciousness goes.

milk.mechanism: Calcium arrives with the lactose and the phosphate that help absorb it. Bone is dismantled and rebuilt lifelong, and the intake decides which of the two is winning.
Riboflavin becomes FAD and FMN, the carriers half of oxidative metabolism runs on. It is destroyed by light in hours, which is the reason milk left clear glass bottles for opaque cartons.

mistletoe.mechanism: Phoratoxins are proteins that interfere with cell function, and the reputation is worse than the record: most reported ingestions of the American plant produce nausea and blurred vision rather than anything grave.

moon.mechanism: The tide is real and it acts on oceans, not on people: the Moon's tidal pull on a human body is smaller than the pull of the wall beside them. No effect on the body has ever been demonstrated.

morel.mechanism: The toxins here are thermolabile, which is the whole difference: a cooked morel is food and a raw one is not. This is the reverse of the death cap, where heat does nothing at all.

mould.mechanism: Spores and fragments small enough to reach the airway, in numbers that rise with damp. The reaction is usually to the spore as an allergen rather than to any toxin, and it is why the housing is treated rather than the person.

mountain.mechanism: The air is the same one-fifth oxygen all the way up; what falls is the pressure driving it into the blood. The body answers by breathing off carbon dioxide, which changes blood pH, and altitude sickness is mostly that adjustment being made too fast.

mud.mechanism: Clostridium tetani spores are ordinary soil organisms, harmless to swallow, and they germinate only where oxygen has been shut out — which a wound packed with mud does for them.

mussel.mechanism: Copper is in cytochrome c oxidase, the last enzyme in the respiratory chain, and in lysyl oxidase, which cross-links collagen. Shellfish concentrate it because their own oxygen carrier, haemocyanin, is built on copper rather than iron.

natto.mechanism: The bacterium that ferments the beans makes menaquinone-7, a long-lived form of vitamin K. Without K the clotting factors are still built and simply do not work — the liver finishes them by adding a carboxyl group, and K is what lets it.

nitrite.mechanism: It oxidises the iron in haemoglobin from ferrous to ferric, and ferric haem does not bind oxygen. The blood goes brown and a pulse oximeter reads normally, because it is measuring the wrong thing.

nitrogen.mechanism: Under pressure it dissolves into the lipid of nerve membranes and interferes with signalling, much as alcohol does — including the part where judgement goes before the diver notices. It reverses completely on ascent.

oak.mechanism: Acorns and oak leaves carry tannins that bind protein — including the protein of a gut lining. Livestock that eat fallen leaves in quantity get kidney damage from it, and the bitterness that keeps most animals off is the tannin doing its job.

oat.mechanism: Manganese is the metal at the centre of the superoxide dismutase inside mitochondria — the enzyme that disposes of the oxygen radicals respiration itself produces. Whole grains carry most of it in the bran.

obsidian.mechanism: A volcanic glass with no crystal structure to stop a fracture, so it parts along a conchoidal break that can end in an edge a few molecules across — sharper than a surgical steel blade, and it cuts before it is felt.

oil.mechanism: Vegetable oils carry tocopherol along with the fat, and it is there for the oil's sake as much as ours: it is the antioxidant that keeps the polyunsaturated bonds from oxidising before they are eaten.

olive_oil.mechanism: Mostly oleic acid, a single double bond that resists oxidising, and it carries tocopherol with it — a fat-soluble antioxidant that sits in cell membranes and takes the hit instead of the lipids around it.

orange.mechanism: Ascorbic acid is the reducing agent two enzymes need to hydroxylate collagen. Supply it and old scars stay closed; withhold it and they reopen in the order they were made.

ore.mechanism: Most ore bodies sit in silicate rock, so crushing and grinding them makes respirable crystalline silica whatever the metal being chased. The lung cannot clear a particle it cannot dissolve.

oxygen.mechanism: The gas a body runs on is also an oxidant. Above about half an atmosphere the lung lining is damaged by the same chemistry that makes it useful, and at higher pressures still it causes seizures.

oxygen_gas.mechanism: The gas a body runs on is also an oxidant, and above about half an atmosphere of it the lung lining is damaged by the same chemistry that makes it useful. At higher pressures still it causes seizures, which is why divers do not breathe it pure.

oyster.mechanism: Zinc holds a whole class of transcription factors in the shape that lets them grip DNA, and the same metal is spent on wound repair and on taste. Oysters carry several times more of it than any other common food.

paper.mechanism: Cellulose is glucose joined by a bond human enzymes cannot open — no mammal makes cellulase. Paper passes through unchanged, which is the same reason plant fibre is called roughage rather than food.

peanut.mechanism: IgE bound to mast cells recognises the protein and the cells degranulate. Nothing about the peanut is harmful; the harm is entirely the response, which is why the amount needed can be a trace.

Around a quarter protein by weight, with more than most nuts, and the fat is mostly monounsaturated. For the great majority of people this is food; the immune reaction on the other row is the exception, not the rule.

petroleum.mechanism: Crude oil and its lighter fractions carry benzene, which the marrow converts into metabolites that damage the cells making blood. That is why the cancer associated with it is leukaemia rather than a cancer of the lung.

phosphate.mechanism: The form phosphorus is actually eaten and used in: in every ATP, every nucleotide, and most of the mineral in bone. Free phosphorus is another matter entirely and is filed separately.

pipe.mechanism: Plumbing is named after lead — plumbum — because lead was soft enough to bend, and soft water standing in a lead pipe takes some of it with it. The metal imitates calcium closely enough to be absorbed by the same transporters and then does none of calcium's jobs.

plank.mechanism: A splinter is a wound that arrives with its own foreign body already inside it, which is why the infection risk is out of proportion to the size of the injury.

plaster.mechanism: Plaster sets by taking water back into the crystal, and that reaction gives out heat. Under a thick cast the heat has nowhere to go, so the skin beneath can be injured while the cast is hardening rather than by anything applied to it.

platinum.mechanism: As unreactive as gold and harder, so it holds an edge and a shape. It sits in pacemaker electrodes and aneurysm coils for exactly that reason: it can be left in a body indefinitely and stay what it was.

poison_hemlock.mechanism: Coniine blocks transmission at the neuromuscular junction, so the paralysis climbs from the legs upward while the mind stays clear. Death is from the diaphragm giving out, which is the detail every account of Socrates preserves.

pokeweed.mechanism: The whole plant is toxic and the root most of all. It is eaten anyway, as poke sallet, by boiling the young leaves and throwing the water away more than once — a preparation that is a confession of what is in them.

pork.mechanism: Thiamin is the cofactor pyruvate dehydrogenase needs, so without it a cell cannot get sugar into the citric acid cycle at all and the tissues that burn the most sugar — nerve and heart — fail first. It sits in the bran of a grain, which is why beriberi followed the milling machine across Asia and not the rice.

pot.mechanism: The clay is not the problem; the glaze is. Lead oxide has been used as a flux since antiquity because it melts low and fires glossy, and an acidic food sitting in that glaze leaches it back out. In commercial ware the lead is bound to silica in a fixed ratio to hold it in place, so the risk now sits with artisanal pottery fired without that oversight and with antique ware where the bond was never good enough.

potato.mechanism: Not much per mouthful, but eaten in the quantities it was eaten in, enough — which is why scurvy retreated across northern Europe as the potato spread, without anyone knowing why.

protein.mechanism: Every food allergy is to a protein, never to a fat or a sugar, because only a protein is large and structured enough for an antibody to recognise. Cooking sometimes changes the shape enough to break that recognition and sometimes does not, which is why one person can eat a baked egg and not a boiled one.

psyllium.mechanism: The husk is mucilage: it takes up many times its own volume in water and stiffens. Swallowed without enough liquid to finish that reaction it can complete it in the oesophagus instead, where the obstruction is what stops the breathing.

ptfe.mechanism: Nothing sticks to it and nothing reacts with it, because the fluorine shell around the carbon chain is about as chemically closed as an organic molecule gets. Solid PTFE passes through a gut unchanged, which is what makes it a vascular graft material.

pumpkin_seed.mechanism: Phenylalanine is converted to tyrosine and from there to dopamine, adrenaline and the pigment in skin and hair. The one inherited condition in which that first conversion fails is why every newborn in most countries has a heel prick.

quartz.mechanism: The mineral itself. Whole crystals are inert; the fraction small enough to reach an alveolus destroys the macrophage that engulfs it and is released again to do it once more.

quinoa.mechanism: The third branched-chain amino acid. Quinoa is named as a complete protein because it does not run short of lysine the way a cereal does — it is not a cereal, but a relative of spinach.

rabies_virus.mechanism: It travels up peripheral nerves to the brain rather than through the blood, which is slow — and is why a vaccine given after exposure can still get there first.

rain.mechanism: Wet clothing loses heat far faster than dry, because water conducts away from the skin what still air would have held against it. Most hypothermia happens well above freezing, in the rain.

resin.mechanism: Colophony, the resin left after turpentine is distilled off, is one of the commonest causes of occupational contact allergy — it is in solder flux, adhesive plaster and violin rosin alike, and the sensitisation is permanent.

rhododendron.mechanism: Grayanotoxins hold sodium channels open, so nerve and muscle cannot reset. They pass into honey made from the flowers, which is the mad honey of classical accounts and the reason this is a hazard of a food rather than of a plant.

rhubarb.mechanism: The stalk is the food and the leaf blade is not. Oxalic acid binds calcium out of the blood and the resulting crystals are deposited in the kidney, which is the organ that has to filter them.

rice.mechanism: Rice is grown in flooded fields, and flooding mobilises arsenic out of the soil in a form the plant takes up readily. It accumulates in the grain rather than the straw, which is why rice carries more of it than any other staple.

river.mechanism: Moving water is the difference. A current a person can stand in can still take their feet away, and cold water does the rest — the danger is almost never the depth.

rod.mechanism: Bar stock: a length of one metal, ground and straightened. Whatever it does to a body is whatever that metal does, and the metals are filed separately.

rope.mechanism: A rope burn is friction, not heat from outside: the fibres running through a grip abrade and heat the skin at once, which is why it takes the top layer off rather than blistering it.

rubber.mechanism: Natural latex carries plant proteins, and repeated skin contact — especially through the powder that used to line gloves — teaches the immune system to answer them. It became an occupational epidemic among health workers, and powdered gloves were withdrawn because of it.

salmon.mechanism: One of the few foods carrying useful vitamin D, which matters at latitudes where the winter sun is too low in the sky to make any in skin at all.

salt.mechanism: Every nerve impulse is a sodium gradient collapsing and being rebuilt, and the body has no way to manufacture the ion. This is why salt was worth trading across deserts.
The other half of the crystal. Chloride is the counter-ion that lets sodium move, and it is also the acid in the stomach: the parietal cell pumps hydrogen out and chloride follows it.

sand.mechanism: Quartz sand is crystalline silica. Whole grains are far too large to breathe; cutting, grinding or blasting makes a fraction that is not, and the lung cannot clear it.

sandstone.mechanism: Sandstone is cemented quartz, so working it produces the same respirable crystalline silica as sand does. This is the oldest recorded occupational disease there is.

sapphire.mechanism: Crystalline aluminium oxide: too hard to abrade and too stable to dissolve. It is used for the windows of implanted devices, where anything that fogged or reacted would end the device.

sauerkraut.mechanism: Lactic acid bacteria off the leaf itself, working in brine that keeps everything else out. The souring is the preservation and the culture at once.

sea.mechanism: Nothing about the water decides this; the person does. The larynx closes reflexively, so the usual mechanism is hypoxia rather than filling, and it is close to silent because breathing takes priority over speech. Whether the same sea is a swim or a drowning turns on whether you can swim, how far the shore is and how cold it is — which is why this is filed as conditional rather than acute.

dial.note: Minutes. The staging is the survival services’ own: one minute, ten minutes, one hour.

stages.label: In the water
stages.what: Whether this is a swim or an emergency is decided by the person and the distance, not by the water.

stages.label: Cold shock
stages.what: The first minute is the dangerous one. An involuntary gasp, then hyperventilation you cannot override — and a gasp underwater is how a strong swimmer drowns in water they could have swum in warm.

stages.label: Hypothermia
stages.what: An hour before the core is cold enough to lose consciousness — which is why 'they were only in the water twenty minutes' is not the reassurance it sounds like.

sea.mechanism: Water takes heat out of a body roughly twenty-five times faster than air at the same temperature. The first minute is the dangerous one and not the hour: cold shock forces a gasp and then hyperventilation, and a gasp underwater is how a strong swimmer drowns in water they could have swum in warm.

seaweed.mechanism: The thyroid needs iodine to build its hormones and has no substitute for it. Seaweed concentrates it out of seawater, which is why coastal diets rarely showed the deficiency that inland ones did.

seed.mechanism: A seed is a packed lunch with a shelf life, so it carries the antioxidant that protects its own stored fat from going rancid — which is the same tocopherol that protects membranes in us.

sesame.mechanism: The complement to the bean. Legumes are short of methionine and seeds are not, and methionine is the amino acid every protein starts with as well as the body's main methyl donor.

sheet_metal.mechanism: A sheared edge is burred and thin, and it parts skin at a pressure a knife would need to be pressed to reach. Most metalwork injuries are from handling stock rather than from any machine.

silica.mechanism: Particles small enough to reach the alveoli are engulfed by macrophages, which the crystalline surface then destroys, releasing the particle again with inflammatory signals. The cycle repeats and the scarring it leaves does not resolve.

silver.mechanism: Silver taken in over years is deposited in the skin as fine particles and reduced by sunlight, exactly as in a photographic emulsion. The blue-grey is permanent — there is no route by which the body removes it.

sky.mechanism: Not a thing but a colour: sunlight scattered by air molecules, blue scattering more than red. There is nothing there to reach a body, and what does reach it is filed under sun.

smoke.mechanism: Wood smoke is mostly particles under 2.5 microns, small enough to pass the airway defences entirely and reach the alveoli. Household cooking smoke remains one of the largest environmental causes of death in the world.

snake.mechanism: Venom is injected rather than eaten, which is the whole distinction from a poison — the gut would destroy most of it. Neurotoxic venoms block the signal between nerve and muscle, which is why they act in minutes.

snow.mechanism: Melting snow against skin takes heat at the latent heat of fusion, which is far more than cold air of the same temperature can. Frostbite is ice crystals forming inside the tissue and tearing the cells from within.

soil.mechanism: Clostridium tetani spores are ordinary soil bacteria and harmless to swallow. They germinate only where oxygen has been shut out, which a deep or crushed wound does for them — which is why a garden scratch is a different question from a garden puncture.

soybean.mechanism: One of the three branched-chain amino acids, and unusual in being burned in muscle rather than sent to the liver first. Soy is one of the few plant proteins with all nine essential ones in usable proportion.

spark.mechanism: A spark is a fragment of metal or stone burning as it flies. It carries very little heat in total, so it does no harm through clothing — and lands hot enough to ignite tinder or scar a cornea.

spear.mechanism: It concentrates the whole force of a throw or a thrust onto a few square millimetres, which is the only reason a person can pierce an animal larger than themselves. Depth, not width, is what makes the wound dangerous.

spinach.mechanism: It does contain iron, but bound up with oxalate, so much less crosses the gut wall than the number on the label suggests. The nineteenth-century arithmetic error that made spinach famous was corrected long before the reputation was.

spring.mechanism: A wound spring is stored energy with no brake on it, and machine guarding exists largely for that class of hazard: released at once, by a failure or a hand in the wrong place, it delivers all of it in the time the coil takes to unwind.

star.mechanism: Every star but one is too far away to matter. The next nearest delivers less energy to a person's skin than a candle across a room, and the Sun is filed separately because it is the exception.

steam.mechanism: It carries its latent heat into the skin as it condenses, delivering far more energy than dry air at the same temperature — which is why a steam burn is deep and a hot-air burn of the same reading often is not.

steel.mechanism: Surgical stainless holds a passive chromium-oxide film that reforms the instant it is scratched, so the metal underneath never meets tissue. That is why bone screws and plates are made of it, and why a knife blade and an implant are the same alloy family.

stone.mechanism: Dense, hard and unyielding, so all the energy of an impact goes into the tissue rather than into deforming what struck it. That is the whole difference between being hit by a stone and by something of the same weight that gives.

straw.mechanism: Mouldy hay and straw carry thermophilic actinomycetes, and breathing them repeatedly teaches the immune system to attack the lung tissue holding them. Farmer's lung is that reaction, and it scars.

sugar.mechanism: The bacteria already on a tooth ferment it to acid within minutes, and that acid dissolves the mineral of the enamel. Frequency matters more than quantity: the enamel remineralises between meals and cannot if there is never a gap.

sulfur.mechanism: Burning sulphur makes sulphur dioxide, which dissolves in the wet lining of the airway to make acid there. The gas is a preservative and a bleach for the same reason it is an irritant.

sulfuric_acid.mechanism: It dehydrates tissue rather than simply burning it, and the reaction gives off heat of its own, so a chemical burn becomes a thermal one at the same time.

sun.mechanism: UVB at the skin splits a cholesterol precursor and the body folds the pieces into a hormone it cannot get reliably from food. It is the only vitamin most people make rather than eat, which is why latitude and season show up in blood tests.

The same wavelengths fuse adjacent bases in the DNA of skin cells into dimers. Almost all are cut out and rebuilt; melanoma grows from the small fraction that is not, in the pigment cells, and the damage counts up over a lifetime rather than resetting between summers.

dial.note: the international standard measure of sunburn-producing UV, and an open-ended scale — the bands are the published ones

stages.label: Low
stages.what: Nothing to protect against, and still enough to work with: ten to thirty minutes on forearms and face builds a day's vitamin D at temperate latitudes in summer.

stages.label: Moderate
stages.what: Melanin is moved up over the nuclei of skin cells like a parasol. A tan is a record of damage already done, not protection banked in advance.

stages.label: High
stages.what: Sunburn can start in under fifteen minutes at this strength. The redness is not the burn arriving — it is the response, hours later, as damaged cells signal, which is why you cannot feel a sunburn while you are getting one.

stages.label: Very high
stages.what: Enough that the epidermis separates. Cells too damaged to repair kill themselves rather than divide, and the peeling is that decision made in bulk.

stages.label: Extreme
stages.what: Nothing more happens today. What has been added is to a lifetime total, and melanoma risk answers that total rather than any one afternoon.

sweet_potato.mechanism: The orange flesh is carotene, and varieties bred for more of it are used specifically where vitamin A deficiency blinds children.

taro.mechanism: Raphides — needles of calcium oxalate that inject rather than dissolve, so the burning is mechanical as much as chemical. Prolonged cooking is what breaks them down, and every traditional preparation of the corm does it.

tea.mechanism: The same adenosine blockade, more slowly: theanine alongside the caffeine changes how quickly it arrives, not what it does.

timber.mechanism: The dust, not the beam. Fine hardwood dust is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen and the cancers are of the nose and sinuses — the first tissue the particles meet and the place they are trapped.

titanium.mechanism: It grows its own oxide skin the instant it meets air, a few nanometres thick and chemically dead, and bone will lay itself down directly against that surface. The property has a name — osseointegration — and it is the reason for every dental implant and hip stem.

tobacco_smoke.mechanism: It carries dozens of established carcinogens into direct contact with the airway lining, repeatedly, over years. The latency is what made the association hard to see and easy to deny.

tofu.mechanism: Threonine goes disproportionately into mucin, the gel that lines the gut, so the intestine spends it faster than any other tissue and a shortage shows up there first.

toxoplasma_gondii.mechanism: Usually unnoticed in a healthy adult. It matters in pregnancy and in immunosuppression, which is the pattern for a whole class of organisms that are only conditionally dangerous.

tree.mechanism: A mature tree holds tonnes of stored energy in its own weight and in the tension of a leaning trunk, and it releases all of it in one direction. Tree work has one of the highest fatality rates of any trade for that reason, and most of the deaths are from being struck rather than from falling.

turkey.mechanism: Tryptophan is the precursor of serotonin and of niacin, and the rarest essential amino acid in food. Turkey is famous for it and is not actually unusual — the sleepiness after the meal is the size of the meal, not the bird.

ultraviolet.mechanism: It has enough energy to fuse adjacent thymine bases in DNA into a dimer the cell must cut out and rebuild. Most are repaired; the damage that accumulates is the small fraction that is not.

vibrio_cholerae.mechanism: Its toxin locks the gut's chloride channels open, so water follows the salt out of the body faster than it can be replaced. Death is from dehydration rather than from the organism, which is why rehydration alone saves most cases.

virus.mechanism: A virus is not alive in any useful sense: it carries instructions and a coat, and the copying is done entirely by the cell it enters. That is why almost nothing kills a virus without also harming the host.

walnut.mechanism: Polyunsaturated fat oxidises easily, and the tocopherol packed alongside it is what keeps it intact long enough to be eaten.

wasp.mechanism: The sting itself is minor. The danger is sensitisation: an earlier sting that caused no symptoms taught the immune system to recognise it, and the next one provokes a response out of all proportion.

water.mechanism: The larynx closes reflexively, so the usual mechanism is hypoxia rather than filling. It is also nearly silent, because breathing takes priority over speech.

Plasma is mostly water, and the volume of it decides the pressure the heart is working against. Thirst is triggered by the concentration of the blood rather than by its volume, which is why it lags behind a real deficit.

water_hemlock.mechanism: Cicutoxin is a GABA antagonist, so it removes the brake rather than pressing anything: the result is violent seizures that begin within an hour. It is a different plant and a different mechanism from poison hemlock despite the shared name.

wheat.mechanism: Gluten is not digested to completion by anyone; in coeliac disease the fragments that remain trigger an immune attack on the lining of the small intestine, which then cannot absorb. It is not an allergy and not an intolerance — it is autoimmune, and the damage is to the person's own gut.

wheel.mechanism: A loaded wheel concentrates the whole weight of a vehicle onto a contact patch the size of a hand. What follows a crush is often worse than the crush: muscle held under pressure releases myoglobin when the pressure comes off, and the kidneys are what fail.

whey.mechanism: Leucine does not only build muscle, it signals: it switches on the pathway that starts protein synthesis, so the same amount arriving quickly does more than the same amount arriving slowly. Whey is the fast fraction of milk protein.

wind.mechanism: Wind does not lower the temperature; it strips away the thin layer of air a body has already warmed and keeps stripping it, so heat leaves faster than it can be made. Below about 35 °C the body stops keeping up, and judgement goes before strength does.

wolf.mechanism: Attacks are genuinely rare — far rarer than the folklore — and the documented cases cluster in rabid animals and in animals habituated to people, which is a fact about circumstances rather than about wolves.

wood.mechanism: The dust, not the plank. Fine hardwood dust is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen, and the cancers are of the nose and sinuses — the first tissue the particles meet and the place they are trapped, which is why the association was found among furniture makers.

wool.mechanism: The prickle is mechanical, not allergic: fibres above about thirty microns are stiff enough to indent the skin and set off the same nerve endings pain uses. Finer wool from the same animal does not do it.

yeast.mechanism: Yeast builds folate for its own DNA synthesis and carries a great deal of it. A body needs the same molecule for the same job, most urgently while a neural tube is closing.

yew.mechanism: Every part but the red aril around the seed carries taxine alkaloids, which act on the heart's conduction. The bright flesh birds eat is the exception, and the seed inside it is not.

yoghurt.mechanism: Live cultures arrive in numbers large enough that some survive the stomach. They do not settle permanently; the effect lasts about as long as the eating does.

zinc.mechanism: The classic cause of metal fume fever: galvanised steel heated hot enough to vaporise its zinc coating. The reaction is to the freshly condensed oxide particles, which is why welding the same metal cold does nothing.

beryllium_disease.mechanism: Not a poisoning but a hypersensitivity: the immune system learns the metal and then attacks the lung tissue holding it, building granulomas that stiffen into fibrosis. Only some people sensitise, and the ore is as capable of it as the refined metal.

alcohol.mechanism: Ethanol enhances GABA and blunts glutamate, and a brain held that way for long enough rebalances to compensate. The dependence is that rebalancing: the same drink no longer does what it did, and stopping leaves the compensation unopposed.

soil_transmitted_helminths.mechanism: Hookworm is the reason this is an anaemia and not just an infection: the adult worm attaches to the intestinal wall and feeds on blood, continuously, for years. The loss is slow enough that a child grows up short of iron rather than acutely ill.

botulism.mechanism: The bacterium itself is harmless to swallow; the toxin it makes in an airless, low-acid, unrefrigerated jar is not. It cleaves the proteins a nerve ending needs to release acetylcholine, so the signal to contract never arrives and the paralysis starts at the face and travels down.

radioactivity.mechanism: Alpha emitters do nothing through skin and everything once inside, because the whole of that energy is deposited in a few cell diameters. Radium is treated by the body as calcium and goes to bone, which is why the dial painters' jaws were the first thing to fail.

strong_oxidizer_acid.mechanism: An oxidiser injures by taking electrons from tissue rather than by acid or alkali: the damage is oxidation of the protein itself, and it continues while the compound remains on the skin.

gi_infection_risk.mechanism: All of these take the same road: something that touched faeces reaches a mouth. What differs is only the dose needed, and for norovirus it is small enough that ordinary handwashing failures are sufficient.

hiv_opportunistic_infections.mechanism: These organisms are already present in many healthy people and held in check by cell-mediated immunity. What changes is not the organism but the count of CD4 cells watching it, which is why the same microbe is unremarkable in one person and fatal in another.

capsaicin_irritant.mechanism: Capsaicin opens TRPV1, the same channel heat opens, so the nerve reports a burn that is not there. It is oil-soluble and stays on skin until something that dissolves fat removes it; water spreads it.

trypanosomiasis_burden.mechanism: The parasite changes its surface coat faster than antibodies can be raised against it, so the immune system is always answering the last version. In the African form it eventually crosses into the brain, which is where the sleeping sickness gets its name.

fire.mechanism: Protein denatures above about 44 °C given long enough, so depth follows temperature and time rather than temperature alone. Burning oil carries far more heat per gram than water and clings, which is why an oil fire scalds where a water splash does not.

lead_toxicity.mechanism: Lead imitates calcium closely enough to be taken up by the same transporters, and then does none of calcium's jobs — it interferes with neurotransmitter release and with the enzymes that build haem. It banks in bone, so the exposure outlasts the source by decades.

liver_fluke_infection.mechanism: The fluke lives in the bile ducts and the chronic irritation of that lining is what makes this a cancer risk rather than only an infection. It can persist in one person for around thirty years.

hexavalent_chromium.mechanism: Chromium(VI) crosses the cell membrane through the sulphate channel, which chromium(III) cannot, and is then reduced inside the cell — generating reactive intermediates against the DNA rather than outside it.

alcohol_carcinogen.mechanism: The liver turns ethanol into acetaldehyde, which binds DNA directly and is itself Group 1. The tissues that see it undiluted first — mouth, pharynx, oesophagus — are the ones where the association is strongest.

processed_meat_carcinogen.mechanism: Nitrite curing salts form N-nitroso compounds in the gut, and smoking adds polycyclic aromatics on top. Group 1 is a statement about the strength of the evidence, not about the size of the risk.

pah_carcinogen_grades.mechanism: The body activates these rather than detoxifying them: an enzyme meant to make them water-soluble produces an epoxide that binds DNA. IARC grades them one by one — benzo[a]pyrene Group 1, others 2A and 2B — so this class carries no single verdict.

raw.mechanism: Neither organism is unusual and neither is certain. What changes with pregnancy, age or immunosuppression is not exposure but what a small dose is able to do once it is inside.

severe_weather.mechanism: Wind does its damage by what it carries rather than by pressure, and moving water by weight: a foot of it moves a car because water weighs a tonne per cubic metre and does not compress.

cyanide_poisoning.mechanism: Cyanide binds cytochrome c oxidase at the end of the respiratory chain, so the cell cannot use the oxygen it already has. The blood stays bright red and the tissue suffocates anyway.

red_meat_probable_carcinogen.mechanism: Haem iron catalyses N-nitroso formation in the gut, and high-temperature cooking adds heterocyclic amines. Group 2A means the evidence is strong in animals and limited in people, which is a different statement from Group 1.

lightning.mechanism: Most of the current flashes over the outside of a body rather than through it, which is why survival is common and burns follow the sweat. The lethal cases are cardiac arrest, and a strike does not need to hit you — ground current travels.
